entities.summary:
The Conservative Party of the United Kingdom, known as the Tories, is one of the world's oldest continuously operating political parties, tracing its origins to the Tory faction of the 17th century and organized as the Conservative Party under Sir Robert Peel in 1834. The party that created the modern welfare state (Disraeli), the National Health Service (Attlee, though Labour), and Brexit (Cameron/May/Johnson), the Conservatives have governed Britain for more than two-thirds of the 20th century.

The Conservative Party's evolution from defending Crown and Church in the 17th century to embracing working-class 'one nation' conservatism under Disraeli, free market Thatcherism in the 1980s, and populist nationalism under Boris Johnson represents the most complete political metamorphosis of any major party. Margaret Thatcher's 1979-1990 government privatized nationalized industries, crushed the trade unions, and created the neoliberal economic consensus that defined global capitalism for a generation.

The Conservatives' support for Brexit in the 2016 referendum — which David Cameron gambled on to resolve internal party divisions — resulted in the UK's departure from the EU. The subsequent turmoil, which saw five Conservative prime ministers in 4 years (May, Johnson, Truss, Sunak), culminated in the Conservatives' catastrophic 2024 election defeat — losing over 200 seats and falling to 121 — their worst result since 1906. Rishi Sunak became both the first British Asian prime minister and the Conservative leader who presided over the party's historic collapse.
